detail: 1x A tool RESULT could relabel its own audit row. Refuted: the stamp is written by server code (access.ts::accessDenied → context.outcome) and withAudit never inspects the returned string; audit-denial.test.ts 'a permitted call carries no marker' pins it.

2x A stale stamp could survive to the next call (pooled context). Refuted for FastMCP 4.16.13: one `tool.execute(args, {...})` inline literal per call (chunk-CFPNOSVW.js:1487), both transports; guarded by the deny→allow-on-one-session cases in access-wiring.test.ts and audit-denial.test.ts.

3x The stamp could land on the session object shared by every call (`context.session` is `this.#auth`). Refuted: accessDenied writes only `context.outcome`; the unit case asserts `session.outcome === undefined` after a refusal.

4x `auditReason` (the internal, agent-naming reason for loop/report/queue denials) could reach a non-admin. Refuted: the caller's envelope is byte-identical (tests); the only reader of the row is /api/audit-log, every route `Depends(require_admin)` (routers/audit_log.py L50-L208 incl. list_audit_log).

5x Reasons could carry secret material into the row. Refuted: every reason is server-composed from agent names, loop ids, 'Report not found' or the #186 uniform string; no credential enters; log redaction unchanged.
6x configureAudit could be reached at runtime to redirect audit posts. Refuted: exported for createServer only (server.ts:432 is the sole non-test call site); no tool or route exposes it.

7x The injected internalApiSecret could leak through logs. Refuted: used only in the X-Internal-Secret header (audit.ts postAudit); on failure only status/statusText are logged; index.ts passes nothing (env default, unchanged behaviour).
8x Marking a thrown backend 403 as `denied` could let a caller forge refusal rows. Excluded: a backend 403 IS an authorization refusal; labelling it is the honest state (Product Quality Bar #4).

9x Additive `denied`/`error` keys could break hash-chain verification of prior rows. Refuted: _compute_hash (platform_audit_service.py:367-386) normalises the stored details at write time; existing rows keep their hashes; new rows hash their own keys.

10x Enumeration (#186) via the row's reason. Refuted: user-scope denials keep the uniform reason; agent-scope reasons name the target the caller itself supplied; only the admin-only row gains a loop's owning agent (see 4).

11x Secret patterns in the diff + new test file. 0 hits (AKIA / sk- / ghp_ / gho_ / github_pat_ / xox / PEM); the only secret-shaped strings are the placeholders 'test-secret', 'test-internal-secret', 'trinity_mcp_test…' in tests; 0 emails/IPs in added lines.
12x Enterprise paid-feature disclosure in the 5 changed docs. Replayed the enterprise-docs-guard PATTERN (228 chars) with Python `re` (BSD grep has no -P): 0 hits.
13x Supply chain / CI / Docker / env. Unchanged in the diff (no package*, .github/, docker*, .env* paths).

14x withAudit now hands `execute` `{}` instead of `undefined` — could a tool treat 'no context' as elevated? Refuted: the only object-level check in the tree is a debug log field (agents.ts:338 `hasContext: !!context`); every auth read is `context?.session`, identical for `{}` and `undefined`.
15x The guard test reads the source tree. Test-time only (node:test), not a runtime surface.
16x One more audit POST per refusal (amplification). Unchanged: the wrapper already posted one row per call; only the row's content changed.
